references.text: God's wrath over Israel's sin with the golden calf, which is the background for the bad news the people hear in Exod 33:4
The continuation of the account where the Lord commands the people to take off their jewelry, and the people obey at Mount Horeb
The people mourned and wept when they heard bad news, a similar reaction to bad tidings
The people mourned deeply when they heard the Lord's rebuking words, parallel to the mourning response in Exodus
Jacob mourned over Joseph and would not be comforted, an example of deep grief in the Torah
The people mourned and fasted when they heard bad news, a similar mourning ritual
Ezekiel was told not to mourn in the usual way, showing normal mourning customs in Israel
An appeal to mourn over sin, showing the connection between grief and repentance
Contrast between the people's genuine repentance (Exodus) and the king's indifference (Jeremiah) upon hearing God's word.
